# Comparison of Location-Stratified and Complete-Event Bootstrap Control Limits

A sensitivity analysis was conducted using all available Equipment B data to evaluate whether preserving the observed within-event relationships among sampling locations materially affects the estimated control limits. The comparison was performed separately for DAR, CAR, and Mic.

For each residue type, ND observations were replaced by the LOD, or by the LOQ when the LOD was unavailable. Each usable observation was then normalized by its corresponding USL
$Z_{tr}=100X_{tr}/\mathrm{USL}_{tr}$, where $Z_{tr}$ denotes the normalized result from sampling location $r$ in cleaning event $t$.

## Location-stratified bootstrap

For every sampling location $r$, define the empirical location stratum $G_r=\{Z_{1r},\ldots,Z_{n_r r}\}$.

For bootstrap replication $b=1,\ldots,B$:

1. Sample one observation $Z_{br}^*$ with replacement from each location stratum $G_r$.
2. Combine the independently sampled location-specific observations to form one synthetic cleaning event.
3. Calculate the synthetic event-level location statistic   $L_b^{(\mathrm{location})}   =\operatorname{median}_r Z_{br}^*$.
4. Calculate the synthetic event-level scale statistic   $S_b^{(\mathrm{location})}  =\operatorname{median}_r |Z_{br}^*-L_b^{(\mathrm{location})}|$.

No smoothing noise is added in this sensitivity analysis. Therefore, the location-stratified bootstrap differs from the complete-event bootstrap only in whether the historical within-event relationships among sampling locations are preserved.

The location-stratified bootstrap control limits are estimated as $UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left\{L_1^{(\mathrm{location})},\ldots,L_B^{(\mathrm{location})}\right\}$,
and $UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left\{S_1^{(\mathrm{location})},\ldots,S_B^{(\mathrm{location})}\right\}$, where $\alpha=1/\mathrm{ARL}_0$.

## Complete-event bootstrap

For each historical cleaning event $t$, calculate $L_t=\operatorname{median}_r Z_{tr}$ and $S_t=\operatorname{median}_r|Z_{tr}-L_t|$.

For bootstrap replication $b=1,\ldots,B$:

1. Sample one complete historical cleaning event with replacement from the available Equipment B events.
2. Retain all sampling-location observations within the selected event as a single unit.
3. Record the corresponding event-level statistics $L_b^{(\mathrm{event})}$ and $S_b^{(\mathrm{event})}$.

This resampling procedure preserves the observed relationships among sampling locations within each historical cleaning event. The complete-event bootstrap control limits are estimated as $UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left\{L_1^{(\mathrm{event})},\ldots,L_B^{(\mathrm{event})}\right\}$, and
$UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left\{S_1^{(\mathrm{event})},\ldots,S_B^{(\mathrm{event})}\right\}$.

## Comparison of bootstrap control limits

The absolute differences between the two bootstrap procedures are defined as $\Delta_L=UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}$ and $\Delta_S=UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}$.

The corresponding percentage differences, using the complete-event bootstrap limits as the reference, are $\Delta_L(\%)=100\frac{UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}}{UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}}$ and $\Delta_S(\%)=100\frac{UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}}{UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}}$.

When $UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}=0$, the percentage difference for the scale limit is undefined and only the absolute difference is reported. Because the bootstrap replications generated by the two procedures have no natural one-to-one correspondence, individual simulated $L_b$ and $S_b$ values are not paired or tested. The sensitivity assessment focuses on the resulting $UCL_L$ and $UCL_S$ values.

```{r bootstrap_event_location_ucl_function}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
bootstrap_event_location_ucl <- function(
    file,

    equipment_label = "Equipment B",
    sheets = c("DAR", "CAR", "Mic"),

    # Bootstrap design
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    B = 20000,
    seed = 123,

    # Input columns
    event_col = "Event",
    location_col = "Location",
    result_col = "Result",
    lod_col = "LOD",
    loq_col = "LOQ",
    usl_col = "USL",

    # Output controls
    keep_bootstrap_statistics = FALSE,
    save_table = FALSE,
    output_file = file.path(
      getwd(),
      "Equipment_B_event_vs_location_bootstrap_UCL.csv"
    )
) {

  # ============================================================
  # 0. Package and argument checks
  # ============================================================

  required_pkgs <- c(
    "readxl",
    "dplyr",
    "stringr",
    "matrixStats"
  )

  missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[
    !(required_pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages()))
  ]

  if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Please install the following package(s): ",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    stop("The input file does not exist: ", file)
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop("target_ARL0 must be greater than 1.")
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop("B must be a positive integer.")
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  available_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(file)

  missing_sheets <- setdiff(
    sheets,
    available_sheets
  )

  if (length(missing_sheets) > 0) {
    stop(
      "The following requested worksheet(s) were not found: ",
      paste(missing_sheets, collapse = ", "),
      ". Available worksheets: ",
      paste(available_sheets, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 1. Helper functions
  # ============================================================

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    x <- x[
      !is.na(x) &
        is.finite(x)
    ]

    if (length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    med_x <- stats::median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    stats::median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  is_nd_result <- function(x) {

    x_chr <- trimws(
      toupper(
        as.character(x)
      )
    )

    x_chr %in% c(
      "ND",
      "N.D.",
      "N/D",
      "NON-DETECT",
      "NONDETECT",
      "NON DETECT",
      "NOT DETECT"
    )
  }

  extract_event_number <- function(x) {

    x_chr <- trimws(
      as.character(x)
    )

    x_num_direct <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(x_chr)
    )

    x_num_extracted <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        stringr::str_extract(
          x_chr,
          "\\d+$"
        )
      )
    )

    dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(x_num_direct) ~ x_num_direct,
      !is.na(x_num_extracted) ~ x_num_extracted,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    x <- x[
      !is.na(x) &
        is.finite(x)
    ]

    if (length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  calculate_percent_difference <- function(
      location_value,
      event_value
  ) {

    if (
      is.na(location_value) ||
      is.na(event_value) ||
      !is.finite(location_value) ||
      !is.finite(event_value) ||
      event_value == 0
    ) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    100 * (
      location_value - event_value
    ) / event_value
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 2. Process one residue worksheet
  # ============================================================

  analyze_one_residue <- function(
      sheet_name,
      sheet_seed
  ) {

    message(
      "Analyzing ",
      equipment_label,
      ": ",
      sheet_name
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.1 Read worksheet
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    dat_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
      path = file,
      sheet = sheet_name
    )

    dat_raw <- dat_raw |>
      dplyr::rename_with(
        ~ stringr::str_trim(.x)
      )

    result_col_actual <- result_col

    if (
      !(result_col_actual %in% names(dat_raw)) &&
        sheet_name %in% names(dat_raw)
    ) {
      result_col_actual <- sheet_name
    }

    required_cols <- c(
      event_col,
      location_col,
      result_col_actual,
      lod_col,
      loq_col,
      usl_col
    )

    missing_cols <- setdiff(
      required_cols,
      names(dat_raw)
    )

    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " is missing required column(s): ",
        paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.2 Replace ND and conduct USL normalization
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    normalized_data <- dat_raw |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Equipment = equipment_label,

        ResidueType = sheet_name,

        Event = extract_event_number(
          .data[[event_col]]
        ),

        Location = trimws(
          as.character(
            .data[[location_col]]
          )
        ),

        Result_chr = trimws(
          as.character(
            .data[[result_col_actual]]
          )
        ),

        ND_flag = is_nd_result(
          Result_chr
        ),

        Result_raw = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(Result_chr)
        ),

        LOD = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[lod_col]]
          )
        ),

        LOQ = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[loq_col]]
          )
        ),

        USL = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[usl_col]]
          )
        ),

        Result_Replacement_Source =
          dplyr::case_when(
            ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~
              "ND replaced by LOD",

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              !is.na(LOQ) ~
              "ND replaced by LOQ",

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              is.na(LOQ) ~
              "Removed: ND with missing LOD and LOQ",

            !ND_flag &
              !is.na(Result_raw) ~
              "Observed Result",

            TRUE ~
              "Removed: missing or nonnumeric Result"
          ),

        Result_ND_Replaced =
          dplyr::case_when(
            ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~
              LOD,

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              !is.na(LOQ) ~
              LOQ,

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              is.na(LOQ) ~
              NA_real_,

            !ND_flag &
              !is.na(Result_raw) ~
              Result_raw,

            TRUE ~
              NA_real_
          )
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(Event),
        !is.na(Location),
        Location != "",
        !is.na(Result_ND_Replaced),
        is.finite(Result_ND_Replaced),
        !is.na(USL),
        is.finite(USL),
        USL > 0
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Normalized =
          100 * Result_ND_Replaced / USL
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(Normalized),
        is.finite(Normalized)
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(
        Event,
        Location
      )

    if (nrow(normalized_data) == 0) {
      stop(
        "No usable observations remain in worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " after preprocessing."
      )
    }

    n_events <- dplyr::n_distinct(
      normalized_data$Event
    )

    n_locations <- dplyr::n_distinct(
      normalized_data$Location
    )

    if (n_events < 2) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " must contain at least two usable events."
      )
    }

    if (n_locations < 1) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " has no usable sampling locations."
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.3 Check the sampling-location structure
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    event_location_structure <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::group_by(Event) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        n_observations = dplyr::n(),

        n_locations =
          dplyr::n_distinct(Location),

        location_set = paste(
          sort(unique(Location)),
          collapse = " | "
        ),

        .groups = "drop"
      )

    n_distinct_location_sets <-
      dplyr::n_distinct(
        event_location_structure$location_set
      )

    if (n_distinct_location_sets > 1) {
      warning(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " contains ",
        n_distinct_location_sets,
        " different event-level sampling-location sets. ",
        "The location-stratified bootstrap forms synthetic events ",
        "using all location strata represented in the worksheet, ",
        "whereas the event bootstrap preserves each historical ",
        "event's original sampling-location set."
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.4 Calculate statistics for complete historical events
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    event_statistics <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::group_by(Event) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        L_t = stats::median(
          Normalized,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

        S_t = mad_unscaled(
          Normalized
        ),

        n_observations = dplyr::n(),

        n_locations =
          dplyr::n_distinct(Location),

        n_ND = sum(
          ND_flag,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

        .groups = "drop"
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(L_t),
        is.finite(L_t),
        !is.na(S_t),
        is.finite(S_t)
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(Event)

    if (nrow(event_statistics) < 2) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " has fewer than two usable complete-event statistics."
      )
    }

    # ==========================================================
    # 3. Unsmoothed location-stratified bootstrap
    # ==========================================================

    location_data <- split(
      normalized_data$Normalized,
      normalized_data$Location
    )

    location_data <- lapply(
      location_data,
      function(z) {
        z[
          !is.na(z) &
            is.finite(z)
        ]
      }
    )

    location_data <- location_data[
      lengths(location_data) > 0
    ]

    location_data <- location_data[
      sort(names(location_data))
    ]

    if (length(location_data) == 0) {
      stop(
        "No valid location strata remain for worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        "."
      )
    }

    set.seed(
      sheet_seed + 1L
    )

    location_bootstrap_matrix <- matrix(
      NA_real_,
      nrow = B,
      ncol = length(location_data)
    )

    colnames(location_bootstrap_matrix) <-
      names(location_data)

    for (r in seq_along(location_data)) {

      z_r <- location_data[[r]]

      # Sample only observed normalized values.
      # No smoothing noise is added.
      location_bootstrap_matrix[, r] <-
        sample(
          x = z_r,
          size = B,
          replace = TRUE
        )
    }

    if (ncol(location_bootstrap_matrix) == 1) {

      L_location_boot <-
        location_bootstrap_matrix[, 1]

      S_location_boot <-
        rep(0, B)

    } else {

      L_location_boot <-
        matrixStats::rowMedians(
          location_bootstrap_matrix,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )

      location_absolute_deviations <-
        abs(
          sweep(
            x = location_bootstrap_matrix,
            MARGIN = 1,
            STATS = L_location_boot,
            FUN = "-"
          )
        )

      S_location_boot <-
        matrixStats::rowMedians(
          location_absolute_deviations,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    }

    UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
      L_location_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
      S_location_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # 4. Complete-event bootstrap
    # ==========================================================

    set.seed(
      sheet_seed + 2L
    )

    sampled_event_rows <- sample.int(
      n = nrow(event_statistics),
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    L_event_boot <-
      event_statistics$L_t[
        sampled_event_rows
      ]

    S_event_boot <-
      event_statistics$S_t[
        sampled_event_rows
      ]

    UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
      L_event_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
      S_event_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # 5. Compare the resulting UCLs
    # ==========================================================

    Delta_UCL_L <-
      UCL_L_location -
      UCL_L_event

    Percent_Delta_UCL_L <-
      calculate_percent_difference(
        location_value = UCL_L_location,
        event_value = UCL_L_event
      )

    Delta_UCL_S <-
      UCL_S_location -
      UCL_S_event

    Percent_Delta_UCL_S <-
      calculate_percent_difference(
        location_value = UCL_S_location,
        event_value = UCL_S_event
      )

    comparison_row <- data.frame(
      ResidueType = sheet_name,

      n_events = nrow(event_statistics),

      n_locations =
        length(location_data),

      n_distinct_event_location_sets =
        n_distinct_location_sets,

      B = B,

      target_ARL0 = target_ARL0,

      alpha = alpha,

      UCL_L_location = UCL_L_location,

      UCL_L_event = UCL_L_event,

      Delta_UCL_L = Delta_UCL_L,

      Percent_Delta_UCL_L =
        Percent_Delta_UCL_L,

      UCL_S_location = UCL_S_location,

      UCL_S_event = UCL_S_event,

      Delta_UCL_S = Delta_UCL_S,

      Percent_Delta_UCL_S =
        Percent_Delta_UCL_S,

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    location_strata_summary <- data.frame(
      ResidueType = sheet_name,

      Location = names(location_data),

      n = lengths(location_data),

      Median = vapply(
        location_data,
        stats::median,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      MAD = vapply(
        location_data,
        mad_unscaled,
        numeric(1)
      ),

      Min = vapply(
        location_data,
        min,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      Max = vapply(
        location_data,
        max,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    details <- list(
      residue_type = sheet_name,

      normalized_data =
        normalized_data,

      event_statistics =
        event_statistics,

      event_location_structure =
        event_location_structure,

      location_strata_summary =
        location_strata_summary,

      UCL_L_location =
        UCL_L_location,

      UCL_S_location =
        UCL_S_location,

      UCL_L_event =
        UCL_L_event,

      UCL_S_event =
        UCL_S_event,

      comparison =
        comparison_row
    )

    if (keep_bootstrap_statistics) {

      details$bootstrap_statistics <- list(
        L_location = L_location_boot,
        S_location = S_location_boot,
        L_event = L_event_boot,
        S_event = S_event_boot
      )

    } else {

      details$bootstrap_statistics <- NULL
    }

    details
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 6. Analyze DAR, CAR, and Mic
  # ============================================================

  residue_results <- lapply(
    seq_along(sheets),
    function(i) {

      analyze_one_residue(
        sheet_name = sheets[i],
        sheet_seed = seed + 1000L * i
      )
    }
  )

  names(residue_results) <- sheets

  comparison_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(
      residue_results,
      function(x) {
        x$comparison
      }
    )
  )

  comparison_table <- comparison_table |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("UCL_"),
        ~ round(.x, 6)
      ),

      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("Delta_"),
        ~ round(.x, 6)
      ),

      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("Percent_Delta_"),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    )

  if (save_table) {

    utils::write.csv(
      x = comparison_table,
      file = output_file,
      row.names = FALSE
    )

    message(
      "Comparison table saved to: ",
      output_file
    )
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 7. Return results
  # ============================================================

  output <- list(
    method =
      paste0(
        "Unsmoothed location-stratified bootstrap versus ",
        "complete-event bootstrap"
      ),

    equipment_label =
      equipment_label,

    file =
      file,

    sheets =
      sheets,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    B =
      B,

    seed =
      seed,

    location_bootstrap_smoothing =
      FALSE,

    delta_definition =
      "Delta = UCL_location - UCL_event",

    percent_delta_definition =
      paste0(
        "Percent Delta = 100 * ",
        "(UCL_location - UCL_event) / UCL_event"
      ),

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table,

    residue_results =
      residue_results,

    output_file = if (save_table) {
      output_file
    } else {
      NA_character_
    }
  )

  class(output) <- c(
    "bootstrap_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(output)
}
```


```{r bootstrap_event_location_ucl_function_run}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
equipment_b_bootstrap_comparison <-
  bootstrap_event_location_ucl(
    file = file1,
    equipment_label = "Equipment B",
    sheets = c("DAR", "CAR", "Mic"),
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    B = 2000000,
    seed = 2345678,
    keep_bootstrap_statistics = FALSE,
    save_table = TRUE
  )
```

```{r tbl-bootstrap-equipment-b}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of location-stratified and complete-event bootstrap upper control limits for Equipment B."
#| tbl-label: tbl-bootstrap-equipment-b

bootstrap_equipment_b_table <-
  equipment_b_bootstrap_comparison$comparison_table |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Residue = ResidueType,
    L_Loc = UCL_L_location,
    L_Evt = UCL_L_event,
    L_Diff = Delta_UCL_L,
    L_DiffPct = Percent_Delta_UCL_L,
    S_Loc = UCL_S_location,
    S_Evt = UCL_S_event,
    S_Diff = Delta_UCL_S,
    S_DiffPct = Percent_Delta_UCL_S
  )

bootstrap_equipment_b_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 4,
    align = c(
      "l",
      rep("r", 8)
    ),
    col.names = c(
      "Residue",
      "Loc.",
      "Event",
      "$\\Delta$",
      "$\\Delta\\%$",
      "Loc.",
      "Event",
      "$\\Delta$",
      "$\\Delta\\%$"
    ),
    escape = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(
      " " = 1,
      "$UCL_L$" = 4,
      "$UCL_S$" = 4
    ),
    escape = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c(
      "scale_down",
      "hold_position"
    ),
    position = "center",
    font_size = 8
  ) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(
    column = 1,
    bold = TRUE
  )
```

# Simulation Procedure for Comparing Complete-Event Simulation and Location-Stratified Bootstrap

A simulation study was conducted to examine whether location-stratified bootstrap resampling can approximate the control limits obtained from complete events when sampling locations are independent.

## Data-generating model

Each cleaning event was assumed to contain measurements from 10 sampling locations. The location measurements were generated independently from normal distributions with location-specific means and a common standard deviation: $X_{tr}\sim N(\mu_r,2^2)$, where $X_{tr}$ represents the observation from location $r$ in event $t$, and
$\mu_r=1+0.1r,\qquad r=1,\ldots,10$. Therefore, the 10 location-specific distributions were $X_{t1}\sim N(1.1,2^2)$, $X_{t2}\sim N(1.2,2^2)$, $\ldots$ $X_{t,10}\sim N(2.0,2^2)$.

Measurements from different sampling locations and different events were generated independently.

For any simulated event $t$, the event-level location and scale statistics were defined as $L_t=\operatorname{median}_{r=1,\ldots,10}X_{tr}$ and $S_t=\operatorname{median}_{r=1,\ldots,10}|X_{tr}-L_t|$. Here, $S_t$ is the unscaled median absolute deviation within event $t$.

## Complete-event simulation

First, 20,000 complete events were generated directly from the specified location distributions. For each simulated event, one observation was independently generated from each of the 10 location-specific normal distributions: $\mathbf{X}_t=(X_{t1},\ldots,X_{t,10})$.

The corresponding event-level statistics $L_t$ and $S_t$ were then calculated for each of the 20,000 simulated events.

Let $\alpha=1/\mathrm{ARL}_0$, where $\mathrm{ARL}_0=740$. The complete-event limits were estimated as $UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left(L_1,\ldots,L_{20000}\right)$
and $UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left(S_1,\ldots,S_{20000}\right)$, where $1-\alpha=1-\frac{1}{740}\approx0.9986486$.

These limits approximate the control limits under the known event-generating model.

## Construction of historical location strata

Separately, a historical reference dataset containing 100 events was generated from the same model. Each historical event contained one observation from each of the 10 sampling locations.

For each sampling location $r$, the 100 historical observations were used to construct an empirical location stratum: $G_r=\{X_{1r},X_{2r},\ldots,X_{100,r}\}$, for $r=1,\ldots,10$.
Thus, $G_r$ represents the empirical distribution of observations from sampling location $r$ based on the 100 historical events.

## Location-stratified bootstrap

A total of $B=20{,}000$ synthetic events were generated using location-stratified bootstrap resampling.

For each bootstrap replication $b=1,\ldots,B$:

1. One observation $X_{br}^*$ was sampled with replacement from each empirical location stratum $G_r$.
2. The 10 independently sampled location values were combined to form one synthetic event:    $\mathbf{X}_b^*=(X_{b1}^*,\ldots,X_{b,10}^*)$.
3. The event-level location statistic was calculated as    $L_b^{(\mathrm{location})}   =   \operatorname{median}_{r=1,\ldots,10}X_{br}^*$.
4. The event-level scale statistic was calculated as   $S_b^{(\mathrm{location})}   =   \operatorname{median}_{r=1,\ldots,10}   |X_{br}^*-L_b^{(\mathrm{location})}|$.

No smoothing noise was added. Therefore, the location-stratified bootstrap sampled only from the empirical location-specific distributions obtained from the 100 historical events.

The location-stratified bootstrap limits were estimated as $UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left(L_1^{(\mathrm{location})},\ldots,L_B^{(\mathrm{location})}\right)$
and $UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}=Q_{1-\alpha}\left(S_1^{(\mathrm{location})},\ldots,S_B^{(\mathrm{location})}\right)$.

## Comparison of control limits

The complete-event simulation and location-stratified bootstrap limits were compared using their absolute differences: $\Delta_L=UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}$
and $\Delta_S=UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}$. The corresponding percentage differences, using the complete-event simulation limits as the reference, were calculated as $\Delta_L(\%)=100\frac{UCL_L^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}}{UCL_L^{(\mathrm{event})}}$ and $\Delta_S(\%)=100\frac{UCL_S^{(\mathrm{location})}-UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}}{UCL_S^{(\mathrm{event})}}$.

Because the sampling locations were generated independently under the specified model, the location-stratified bootstrap was expected to approximate the complete-event simulation. Any observed differences between the two procedures can be attributed primarily to the finite size of the 100-event historical reference dataset and Monte Carlo variation in estimating the extreme $(1-1/740)$ quantile.

A fixed random-number seed was used to ensure reproducibility.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

simulate_event_location_ucl <- function(
    n_historical_events = 100,
    n_locations = 10,
    location_means = seq(1.1, 2.0, by = 0.1),
    location_sd = 2,
    n_simulated_events = 20000,
    B = 20000,
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    seed = 123
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Argument checks
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(location_means) != n_locations) {
    stop(
      "The length of location_means must equal n_locations."
    )
  }

  if (n_historical_events < 1) {
    stop("n_historical_events must be positive.")
  }

  if (n_simulated_events < 1) {
    stop("n_simulated_events must be positive.")
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop("B must be positive.")
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop("target_ARL0 must be greater than 1.")
  }

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: unscaled MAD used in the CCSSBU procedure
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    med_x <- median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1. Generate 100 historical events.
  #
  # Each row represents one event.
  # Each column represents one sampling location.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed)

  historical_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_historical_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    historical_data[, r] <- stats::rnorm(
      n = n_historical_events,
      mean = location_means[r],
      sd = location_sd
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 2. Simulate complete events directly from the known
  # location distributions.
  #
  # Because the locations are generated independently, each row
  # represents a complete event from the known event-generating
  # mechanism.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  simulated_event_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_simulated_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(simulated_event_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    simulated_event_data[, r] <- stats::rnorm(
      n = n_simulated_events,
      mean = location_means[r],
      sd = location_sd
    )
  }

  L_event <- apply(
    simulated_event_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_event <- apply(
    simulated_event_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
    L_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
    S_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3. Construct G_1,...,G_10 from the 100 historical events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  location_strata <- lapply(
    seq_len(n_locations),
    function(r) {
      historical_data[, r]
    }
  )

  names(location_strata) <- colnames(
    historical_data
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 4. Location-stratified empirical bootstrap.
  #
  # Sample one observation from each G_r and combine the sampled
  # values into a synthetic event. No smoothing noise is added.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 1L)

  location_bootstrap_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(location_bootstrap_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    location_bootstrap_data[, r] <- sample(
      x = location_strata[[r]],
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )
  }

  L_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
    L_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
    S_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 5. Compare the UCLs.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  Delta_L <-
    UCL_L_location -
    UCL_L_event

  Delta_S <-
    UCL_S_location -
    UCL_S_event

  Percent_Delta_L <-
    100 * Delta_L / UCL_L_event

  Percent_Delta_S <-
    100 * Delta_S / UCL_S_event

  comparison_table <- data.frame(
    Statistic = c(
      "L",
      "S"
    ),

    UCL_event = c(
      UCL_L_event,
      UCL_S_event
    ),

    UCL_location = c(
      UCL_L_location,
      UCL_S_location
    ),

    Delta = c(
      Delta_L,
      Delta_S
    ),

    Percent_Delta = c(
      Percent_Delta_L,
      Percent_Delta_S
    ),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return all useful objects.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  result <- list(
    seed = seed,

    n_historical_events =
      n_historical_events,

    n_locations =
      n_locations,

    location_means =
      location_means,

    location_sd =
      location_sd,

    n_simulated_events =
      n_simulated_events,

    B =
      B,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    historical_data =
      historical_data,

    location_strata =
      location_strata,

    simulated_event_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_event = L_event,
        S_event = S_event
      ),

    location_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_location = L_location,
        S_location = S_location
      ),

    UCL_L_event =
      UCL_L_event,

    UCL_S_event =
      UCL_S_event,

    UCL_L_location =
      UCL_L_location,

    UCL_S_location =
      UCL_S_location,

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table
  )

  class(result) <- c(
    "simulate_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(result)
}
```

The following output shows stratified location level bootstrap UCL is more conservative than event level bootstrap UCL

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
simulation_result <- simulate_event_location_ucl(
  n_historical_events = 100,
  n_locations = 10,
  location_means = seq(1.1, 2.0, by = 0.1),
  location_sd = 2,
  n_simulated_events = 20000,
  B = 20000,
  target_ARL0 = 740,
  seed = 123
)

```


# Multivaraite Simulation

## Simulation Algorithm for Comparing Event-Level and Location-Stratified Bootstrapping

A simulation study was conducted to compare control limits obtained from event-level statistics and location-stratified bootstrapping under a correlated-location model.

**Step 1. Generate historical events**

Generate 100 complete historical events from the random-effects model $X_{ir}=\mu_r+E_i+\varepsilon_{ir}$, where $i=1,\ldots,100$ denotes the event index and $r=1,\ldots,10$ denotes the sampling location.

The location means were specified as $\mu_r \in \{1.1,1.2,\ldots,2.0\}$. The event effects and residual errors were generated independently from $E_i \sim N(0,1)$ and $\varepsilon_{ir} \sim N(0,3)$. Consequently, each location had marginal variance $\operatorname{Var}(X_{ir})=4$ and standard deviation 2, while the within-event correlation between any two locations was $\operatorname{Corr}(X_{ir},X_{is})=0.25$.

**Step 2. Calculate the observed event statistics**

For each of the 100 simulated events, calculate $L_t=\operatorname{median}(X_{t1},\ldots,X_{t10})$ and $S_t=\operatorname{MAD}(X_{t1},\ldots,X_{t10})$, where MAD denotes the unscaled median absolute deviation. This produced 100 observed values of $L_t$ and 100 observed values of $S_t$.

**Step 3. Construct empirical location strata**

Using the 100 complete historical events, construct ten empirical location strata, $G_1,\ldots,G_{10}$, where $G_r$ contains all observations collected from location $r$. Each stratum therefore contained 100 observations.

**Step 4. Perform location-stratified bootstrapping**

For each bootstrap replication:

1. Sample one observation with replacement from each stratum $G_r$.
2. Combine the ten sampled observations into a synthetic event.
3. Calculate the corresponding bootstrap statistics $L_t^{(b)}$ and $S_t^{(b)}$.

Repeat this procedure 200,000 times.

The resulting bootstrap distributions were used to estimate $UCL_{L,\text{Location}}$ and $UCL_{S,\text{Location}}$ at the probability level $1-1/740$.

**Step 5. Perform event-level bootstrapping**

For each bootstrap replication:

1. Sample one of the 100 observed events with replacement.
2. Record the corresponding observed event statistics $L_t$ and $S_t$.

Repeat this procedure 200,000 times. The resulting bootstrap distributions were used to estimate $UCL_{L,\text{Event}}$ and $UCL_{S,\text{Event}}$ at the probability level
$1-1/740$.

**Step 6. Compare control limits**

The two approaches were compared using $\Delta_L = UCL_{L,\text{Location}}-UCL_{L,\text{Event}}$ and $\Delta_S = UCL_{S,\text{Location}}-UCL_{S,\text{Event}}$. Percentage differences were calculated as $\Delta_L\% = 100\times\Delta_L/UCL_{L,\text{Event}}$ and $\Delta_S\% = 100\times\Delta_S/UCL_{S,\text{Event}}$.

Negative values indicate that the location-stratified bootstrap produced a more conservative control limit than the event-level bootstrap.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

simulate_event_location_ucl <- function(
    n_historical_events = 100,
    n_locations = 10,
    location_means = seq(1.1, 2.0, by = 0.1),
    event_variance = 1,
    residual_variance = 3,
    B = 200000,
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    seed = 123
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Argument checks
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(location_means) != n_locations) {
    stop(
      "The length of location_means must equal n_locations."
    )
  }

  if (n_historical_events < 2) {
    stop(
      "n_historical_events must be at least 2."
    )
  }

  if (n_locations < 2) {
    stop(
      "n_locations must be at least 2."
    )
  }

  if (event_variance < 0) {
    stop(
      "event_variance cannot be negative."
    )
  }

  if (residual_variance <= 0) {
    stop(
      "residual_variance must be positive."
    )
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop(
      "B must be positive."
    )
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop(
      "target_ARL0 must be greater than 1."
    )
  }

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  marginal_variance <-
    event_variance +
    residual_variance

  marginal_sd <-
    sqrt(marginal_variance)

  within_event_correlation <-
    event_variance /
    marginal_variance

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: unscaled MAD used in the CCSSBU procedure
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    med_x <- median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1. Generate 100 correlated historical events.
  #
  # Model:
  #
  # X_ir = mu_r + E_i + epsilon_ir,
  #
  # where
  #
  # E_i ~ N(0, event_variance)
  #
  # and
  #
  # epsilon_ir ~ N(0, residual_variance).
  #
  # Each row is one complete event.
  # Each column is one sampling location.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed)

  event_effects <- stats::rnorm(
    n = n_historical_events,
    mean = 0,
    sd = sqrt(event_variance)
  )

  residual_errors <- matrix(
    stats::rnorm(
      n = n_historical_events * n_locations,
      mean = 0,
      sd = sqrt(residual_variance)
    ),
    nrow = n_historical_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  historical_data <-
    residual_errors +
    event_effects +
    matrix(
      location_means,
      nrow = n_historical_events,
      ncol = n_locations,
      byrow = TRUE
    )

  colnames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  rownames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Event_",
    seq_len(n_historical_events)
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 2. Calculate the observed L_t and S_t values for the
  # 100 historical events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  L_observed <- apply(
    historical_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_observed <- apply(
    historical_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  observed_event_statistics <- data.frame(
    Event = seq_len(n_historical_events),
    L = L_observed,
    S = S_observed
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3. Construct G_1,...,G_10 from the 100 historical
  # events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  location_strata <- lapply(
    seq_len(n_locations),
    function(r) {
      historical_data[, r]
    }
  )

  names(location_strata) <- colnames(
    historical_data
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 4. Location-stratified bootstrap.
  #
  # For each bootstrap replication, sample one observation from
  # each G_r. The 10 independently sampled location values are
  # combined to form one synthetic event.
  #
  # This procedure preserves each empirical location
  # distribution but does not preserve the within-event
  # dependence in the original data.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 1L)

  location_bootstrap_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(location_bootstrap_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    location_bootstrap_data[, r] <- sample(
      x = location_strata[[r]],
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )
  }

  L_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
    L_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
    S_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 5. Event-level bootstrap.
  #
  # Resample the 100 observed event indices with replacement.
  # The corresponding L_t and S_t values remain paired.
  #
  # Each sampled index therefore represents one resampled
  # complete historical event.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 2L)

  event_bootstrap_indices <- sample(
    x = seq_len(n_historical_events),
    size = B,
    replace = TRUE
  )

  L_event <- L_observed[
    event_bootstrap_indices
  ]

  S_event <- S_observed[
    event_bootstrap_indices
  ]

  UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
    L_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
    S_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 6. Compare the location-stratified and event-level UCLs.
  #
  # Delta < 0 means that the location-stratified bootstrap gives
  # a smaller UCL than the event-level bootstrap.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  Delta_L <-
    UCL_L_location -
    UCL_L_event

  Delta_S <-
    UCL_S_location -
    UCL_S_event

  Percent_Delta_L <-
    100 * Delta_L /
    UCL_L_event

  Percent_Delta_S <-
    100 * Delta_S /
    UCL_S_event

  comparison_table <- data.frame(
    Statistic = c(
      "L",
      "S"
    ),

    UCL_event = c(
      UCL_L_event,
      UCL_S_event
    ),

    UCL_location = c(
      UCL_L_location,
      UCL_S_location
    ),

    Delta = c(
      Delta_L,
      Delta_S
    ),

    Percent_Delta = c(
      Percent_Delta_L,
      Percent_Delta_S
    ),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 7. Calculate the empirical covariance and correlation
  # matrices of the 10 locations.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  empirical_covariance <-
    stats::cov(
      historical_data
    )

  empirical_correlation <-
    stats::cor(
      historical_data
    )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return all useful objects.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  result <- list(
    seed =
      seed,

    n_historical_events =
      n_historical_events,

    n_locations =
      n_locations,

    location_means =
      location_means,

    event_variance =
      event_variance,

    residual_variance =
      residual_variance,

    marginal_variance =
      marginal_variance,

    marginal_sd =
      marginal_sd,

    theoretical_within_event_correlation =
      within_event_correlation,

    B =
      B,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    historical_data =
      historical_data,

    event_effects =
      event_effects,

    location_strata =
      location_strata,

    observed_event_statistics =
      observed_event_statistics,

    location_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_location = L_location,
        S_location = S_location
      ),

    event_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_event = L_event,
        S_event = S_event
      ),

    empirical_covariance =
      empirical_covariance,

    empirical_correlation =
      empirical_correlation,

    UCL_L_event =
      UCL_L_event,

    UCL_S_event =
      UCL_S_event,

    UCL_L_location =
      UCL_L_location,

    UCL_S_location =
      UCL_S_location,

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table
  )

  class(result) <- c(
    "simulate_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(result)
}
```

```{r simulation_run}

#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
simulation_result <- simulate_event_location_ucl(
  n_historical_events = 100,
  n_locations = 10,
  location_means = seq(
    1.1,
    2.0,
    by = 0.1
  ),
  event_variance = 1,
  residual_variance = 3,
  B = 200000,
  target_ARL0 = 740,
  seed = 123
)
```

This gives $X_{ir}=\mu_r+E_i+\varepsilon_{ir},$ where $E_i\sim N(0,1)$ and $\varepsilon_{ir}\sim N(0,3).$ Therefore, $\operatorname{Var}(X_{ir})=1+3=4$ and the marginal standard deviation remains
$\operatorname{SD}(X_{ir})=2.$

For two different locations $r\neq s$ from the same event, $\operatorname{Cov}(X_{ir},X_{is})=1$ and $\operatorname{Corr}(X_{ir},X_{is})=\frac{1}{4}=0.25.$

Thus, the simulation preserves the original marginal variance $2^2$ while introducing moderate positive within-event correlation.


```{r tbl-bootstrap-simulation}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "Event-level and location-stratified bootstrap control limits under a correlated-location normal model."
#| tbl-label: tbl-bootstrap-simulation

simulation_table <-
  simulation_result$comparison_table |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Statistic = c(
      "$L$",
      "$S$"
    )
  )

simulation_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 4,
    align = c(
      "l",
      rep("r", 4)
    ),
    col.names = c(
      "Stat.",
      "$UCL_{\\mathrm{event}}$",
      "$UCL_{\\mathrm{loc}}$",
      "$\\Delta$",
      "$\\Delta\\%$"
    ),
    escape = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c(
      "scale_down",
      "hold_position"
    ),
    position = "center",
    font_size = 8
  )
```

## Important statistical interpretation

There is one important limitation that should be stated correctly.

With only 100 observed event-level values, the event bootstrap distribution contains only the original 100 distinct $L_t$ values and 100 distinct $S_t$ values. Resampling 200,000 times does **not** create new values. Because $1-\frac{1}{740}=0.9986486,$

the estimated event-level UCL will generally be the observed maximum: $UCL_{L,\mathrm{event}}\approx\max_{t=1,\ldots,100}L_t,$ and $UCL_{S,\mathrm{event}}\approx\max_{t=1,\ldots,100}S_t.$

By contrast, location-stratified resampling can create many new combinations of location values. Therefore, it produces a much richer synthetic-event distribution. This difference is not a coding problem. It is an inherent consequence of estimating a $0.99865$ quantile from only 100 complete events using a nonsmoothed empirical event-level bootstrap.
